stimulus.text:
Radio in the United States, 1922–1930:

| Year | Licensed radio stations | Homes with a radio |
| 1922 | about 30 | fewer than 1 in 100 |
| 1923 | about 570 | 1 in 100 |
| 1930 | 618 | 40 in 100 |

Source: Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.7 (almost 600 licensed stations by 1923); Proceedings of the IEEE, 2012 (stations and household ownership); “Radio in the United States” (1 percent of homes in 1923).

stem: Which development best explains why the number of stations rose so fast after 1922?

options.text: Congress banned all private radio stations outright
options.misconception: Congress did not ban private stations. The government licensed them, and private companies ran them.

options.text: Radio gave firms a way to sell sets
Farmers asked the government for fewer programs
options.misconception: Farm programs had nothing to do with the station boom. Stations grew because companies saw a market, not because farmers asked for less.

options.text: The government owned every radio station itself
options.misconception: The government did not own the stations. Private firms like Westinghouse owned and ran them.

rationales.A: Congress did not ban private stations. The government licensed them, and private companies ran them.
rationales.B: Background: Westinghouse built KDKA to give people a reason to buy its radio sets, and stores and newspapers ran stations for the same reason. Selling sets drove the station boom.
rationales.C: Farm programs had nothing to do with the station boom. Stations grew because companies saw a market, not because farmers asked for less.
rationales.D: The government did not own the stations. Private firms like Westinghouse owned and ran them.
rationales.general:
1. Ask who built the stations: companies, stores, and newspapers, not the government.
2. Ask why they paid for them: a station gave people a reason to buy a radio set.
3. Connect the motive to the table: the rush to sell sets explains the rush to build stations.
Remember: when a new medium spreads fast, ask who profits from the spread.
